title: Staged bastion bridge and rollback playbook for air-gapped on-prem upgrades
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers with air-gapped or heavily firewalled on-prem environments have requested a low-risk upgrade path that avoids long maintenance windows and supports fast rollback without requiring an open persistent proxy. Existing 'edge bridge' patterns are too permissive for some customers, and fully offline upgrade paths lengthen time-to-recovery when a rollout reveals incompatibilities.

Goal: Define a staged 'bastion bridge' pattern and a companion rollback playbook suitable for customers who require transient, auditable, customer-owned connectivity during a controlled upgrade. Deliverables: 1) playbook template for customer-facing runbooks; 2) automation checklist for SEs/CS; 3) telemetry and gating signals to enable safe automated rollouts; 4) rollback orchestration steps that minimize state drift and data exposure.

Scope: Non-bug product work focused on Private/VPC/on-prem upgrades where networking constraints or air-gap policies prohibit persistent outbound tunnels. This ticket covers the PM-owned runbook and acceptance criteria; implementation work (automation, infra changes) will be split into child ENG tickets.

Out of scope: Full implementation of bastion automation or changes to third-party customer firewalls. This ticket does not change platform security posture or create always-on proxies.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Customer-owned transient bastions reduce our attack surface but require robust validation steps on customer side. 2) Short-lived connectivity windows reduce operational risk but increase coordination complexity. 3) Heavier preflight checks increase lead time; lighter checks risk mid-rollout failures and larger rollbacks.

Key contacts and artifacts: Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Bastion+Bridge+Playbook (internal) | Draft PR for SE scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-scripts/pull/342 | Example customer comms template (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0B-bastion-templates
acceptance_criteria: Runbook covers preflight, connectivity window orchestration, monitoring, rollback trigger criteria, and post-rollback verification
Playbook includes at least two validated rollback scenarios with step-by-step commands and expected outputs
SE checklist reduces median coordination time for a single-customer transient window to under 3 hours (pilot target)
Telemetry signals (connection success, model endpoint health, token-level latency spike) are defined and owned by Console team
Security review completed with Security & Compliance and documented exceptions recorded in ticket
Customer-facing communication templates and consent checklists appended to playbook
runbook_steps: Preflight: collect customer network matrix, target nodes, and KV cache persistence requirements
Agreement: obtain signed transient-bridge consent and maintenance window confirmation
Customer bastion setup: customer provisions an ephemeral bastion host in a DMZ/VLAN with restricted outbound egress to Redwood upgrade IPs
Connectivity test: SE runs scripted validation to verify TLS handshake, expected ports, and minimal bandwidth for model KV sync
Staged rollout: 1% traffic to upgraded binary or model on isolated tenant; monitor gating signals for 30 minutes
Expand rollout: 10% > 50% > 100% with 15m stable windows between each expansion, abort criteria defined
Rollback: failover to pinned model/version in Dedicated pool and revoke bastion access; run verification checks
Post-rollback: collect logs, create RCA, and notify customer with remediation timeline
telemetry_and_gates: Connection success rate >= 99% during connectivity window
Per-route 95th percentile latency does not increase > 25% vs baseline
Error rate (5xx) stays below 0.5% absolute increase
KV cache miss rate within expected bounds (defined per-customer profile)
Automated abort on critical alerts with documented on-call escalation path
